name: TaskRecallerService
src_typeComment: Runs automatically, no wiring needed — records what you were looking at (Hierarchy/Project selection), which scripts you opened, and detects when you've come back after a real gap so the "Task Recaller" window can offer to show itself instead of you having to remember it exists.  What this CANNOT see, on purpose left as an honest gap rather than faked: your actual code editor's open tabs/cursor position (Unity has no API into VS Code/Rider internals — only that you double-clicked a script to open it), and Inspector micro-state like an expanded foldout or an unsaved field edit. The manual note field in the window is the intended answer to that second gap.

src_members.sig: public static bool OnOpenAsset(int instanceId, int line)
src_members.name: OnOpenAsset
src_members.comment: [OnOpenAsset] fires when the user double-clicks an asset to open it — the real, documented hook for "what did they just open," not a guess based on polling. Returning false lets Unity's normal open-in-external-editor behaviour still happen; this only ever observes.
